title: Brute Force and Improve the Approach
learningObjectives: Build a direct baseline approach to a problem.
Recognize how input size affects brute-force work.

understand.concept: Brute force is a direct, systematic approach that checks candidates or possibilities using straightforward logic. It can be a valuable first solution because it is easy to explain and verify, but it may become inefficient as input size grows.
understand.whyItMatters: A simple correct baseline helps establish expected behavior, supports testing, and gives a reference when evaluating more advanced approaches.
understand.analogy: Searching every drawer in a room in order until the missing item is found.
understand.analogyLimit: Brute-force search may be practical for small inputs or when worst-case work is acceptable, but exhaustive checks can grow prohibitively for large problems.

explain.narrative: First identify the candidate space and a clear check. Visit candidates systematically, record matches, and use an early exit when further checks cannot change the needed result. Verify the baseline on small cases, then consider reducing duplicate or unnecessary work, using better data structures, or exploiting problem properties.

examples.title: Simple linear search
examples.explanation: Checking each element in order is a simple brute-force approach.

examples.title: Brute-force pair check
examples.code: const nums=[2,3,5]; let found=false; for(let i=0;i<nums.length;i++){for(let j=i+1;j<nums.length;j++){if(nums[i]+nums[j]===8)found=true;}} console.log(found);
examples.explanation: Every distinct pair is checked until the target sum is found.

examples.title: Compare approaches conceptually
examples.explanation: More data can make a brute-force method perform more checks.

examples.title: Use early exit
examples.code: const values=[1,3,8,9]; let found=false; for(const v of values){if(v===8){found=true;break;}} console.log(found);
examples.explanation: Stopping when a match is found avoids unnecessary remaining checks.

examples.title: Verify brute-force result
examples.explanation: The simple method can be checked against a small known case.

commonMistakes: Forgetting edge cases such as empty input.
Continuing after a result when early exit is safe.
Optimizing before a baseline is verified.
Assuming a simple method scales to large inputs.

guidedTask.title: Guided practice: Find a target value
guidedTask.instructions: Use a straightforward sequential search and trace it.
steps: Choose a short list and target value.
Stop at a match or at the end.
Test the target missing from the list.
guidedTask.starterCode: // Write a trace or pseudocode. No playground is required.

independentTask.title: Independent practice: Find a pair with a target sum
independentTask.instructions: Design a brute-force approach that checks pairs in a small list.
requirements: Avoid pairing an element with itself.
Trace checks until a pair is found or exhausted.
Test a list with no matching pair.
Suggest one improvement and explain its trade-off.

hints: Define exactly what makes a candidate valid.
Trace the comparisons to verify correctness.
Consider early exit or reducing repeated work only after correctness is clear.
